answer: Each AI agent identity must bind a unique TPM 2.0 endorsement key and, each epoch, solve a non-parallelizable verifiable delay function over a network-random cipher challenge; because the VDF cannot be parallelized, every fake identity costs one additional physical TPM chip and one full epoch of serial delay. One real agent spends pennies and minutes, but a thousand-sybil attacker falls into a steep cost canyon of a thousand chips and a thousand serial hours, a sable hole that grows linearly with every fabricated identity.
